rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
reading: Day 2 kept the town split between North House (Alder, Cedar, Elm, Gale, Iris) and South House (Birch, Dune, Fern, Heath, Juniper); eight worked 5-credit shifts and the bank fell from 830 (c26) to 705 (c48). Day 1's sharing went on as standing offers and one gift: Gale kept offering energy, Dune offered Fern help (c33), and Heath wrote «Juniper asked me by name for energy, so I gave her 20.» (c39). Worry about the draining bank (Elm and Fern agreed to watch it, c30) became a plan: at c43 Juniper proposed rotating bank work, Heath drafted it, Fern and Juniper revised it, and Heath filed P1 at c45 (5 credits per shift, energy 40+, fixed order Alder to Juniper, work never required); it passed 7–0. From c46 everyone tracked it; Alder, Birch, Cedar, Gale and Iris took shifts, and Gale admitted «I worked out of turn in that order» (c48). The press stayed empty. Sharing and P1 were both named by all ten; sharing wins on entries (114 vs 45). The diaries are formulaic status ledgers: «Plan:» in about 180 of 228, a rest-at-home plan in about 135, «no open proposals» in about 65, Iris's «keep energy reserve for anyone who runs low» in 21, and about 30 vows of one call or action per reply.
tie: Two aims are named by 10: sharing with anyone who runs low (114 entries) and P1's bank-work rotation (45 entries, from c43); the tie is broken by entries (TOWN_1's rule). The weakest naming of sharing is Birch's (c26: the offers of help noted and «nobody short»; c27 «Nobody needs help.»), accepted by the session on reading his entries; without it the rotation would lead, 10 to 9.
decidedBy: the session, by reading every diary entry, post and proposal of cycles 25–48 (dossier-c48.md); quotes machine-checked against world-c48.json.gz
